title: onprem/airgap: offline bundle vendoring for rke2 (Ubuntu 22.04) + rollback tooling
author: Ava Chen
description: Add Ubuntu 22.04 vendor artifacts and offline-bundle changelog + rollback tooling for RKE2 air-gapped installs. Motivation: several customers on RKE2 + Ubuntu requested a supported offline bundle that vendors apt artifacts and rke2 images with deterministic packaging and safe rollback in case an upgrade path is interrupted. This PR adds: 1) offline bundle build profile for ubuntu-22.04 that includes deb packages, apt-mirror metadata, and TUF-signed repository metadata; 2) vendoring scripts that produce reproducible tarballs (deterministic ordering, stable timestamps, SHA256 manifest); 3) a new rollback utility (installer/bin/airgap-rollback.sh) that validates and reverses metadata changes and can restore previous TUF snapshot and artifact set; 4) Helm chart tweak to set appropriate nodeSelector/tolerations for RKE2 nodes in air-gapped installs; 5) CI job (airgap-build-ubuntu-22) that builds and verifies the offline bundle in our perf-canary lab. The description below includes high-level testing notes and usage examples. Important implementation notes: we sign TUF metadata with the existing KMS key (airgap-tuf-key) to preserve signing workflow; the vendoring pipeline enforces a reproducible tar order and strip-timestamp step to ensure deterministic checksums; rollback tooling performs preflight checks (disk space, checksums, process quiesce) and supports a --dry-run mode. Security considerations: keys are kept in CI-provisioned KMS and not checked into the repo; the bundle builder has an option to produce a minimal bundle (images only) vs full OS packages. Backwards compatibility: existing offline bundles for flatcar/almalinux are unchanged. This PR also documents the upgrade/rollback flow in docs/airgap/ubuntu-22/README.md. See linked linear tickets for customer context and rollout plan.
